content:
OpenAI is adding a new way for ChatGPT and Codex to learn and remember what you do on your Mac, even when the actions take place outside the app itself.

The ChatGPT computer use history is an upgraded replacement for Codex's Chronicle research preview feature.

The new "computer use history" feature builds a searchable timeline from activity across user-selected apps and websites.

OpenAI announced the "computer use history" feature in a desktop app changelog released on Thursday. The feature is off by default and must be enabled by the user, giving people control over which sources are included in the history.

This release comes about a month after ChatGPT for desktop was added to Codex, and follows OpenAI's earlier launch of the experimental Chronicle feature.

OpenAI said that "computer use history" effectively replaces the Chronicle research preview feature, but stressed that this is a rebuilt system, not just a rename.

Chronicle relied on screenshots, whereas "computer use history" uses macOS accessibility features to log interaction events, including clicks, typing, keyboard shortcuts, and switching between different apps.

Here's how OpenAI describes the new feature:

"Computer use history" is an opt-in feature in the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS that turns activity across multiple apps and websites into memories and a timeline for ChatGPT and Codex to use. Users can choose which apps and websites contribute data, pause activity collection, and review or delete usage history at any time. "Computer use history" is available to ChatGPT Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. Business and Enterprise admins must enable the relevant access permissions before workspace members can turn the feature on. Initial availability excludes the European Economic Area (EEA), Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

OpenAI also explained how eligible users can enable the opt-in "computer use history" feature:

Users can ask what they were doing before a break, retrieve recently viewed documents, or organize a summary of the day's work. ChatGPT may also suggest turning repeated workflows into skills or automations.

"Computer use history" and privacy

According to OpenAI, ChatGPT's "computer use history" feature does not capture screenshots, screen recordings, microphone input, or system audio, and browsing activity in incognito mode is likewise not included.

Users can review timeline items in the settings page, show individual memory files in Finder, delete specific items, or clear activity from the last 10 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day, or all time.

"Computer use history" temporarily stores interaction events on the Mac for up to 48 hours. OpenAI says these events are processed on its servers to generate memories, but are not retained afterwards and are not used to train models. The resulting plain-text memory files are stored locally until the user deletes them.

OpenAI also cautioned that "computer use history" may increase the risk of prompt injection attacks because of malicious content within apps or websites. It recommends pausing activity collection when communicating with other people without their explicit consent, and excluding apps that handle sensitive information.
